diagnosis.root_cause: The subscriber ONU on EPON0/3:1 is definitely offline: the live probe responds but reports online=0, auth_flag=Unauth, and MPCP DEREG. All other probed ONUs on EPON0/3 are online with healthy optical levels, so this is not a PON, splitter, OLT, or shared-fibre fault. The all-PON critical alarm is a false monitoring result, not the underlying customer fault.
evidence: The OLT ping, SNMP, OID subtree, CPU, memory, temperature, and uptime are normal, so this is not an OLT failure.
The live probe gives a definite offline result for the subscriber ONU: responds=true and online=0; its authentication state is Unauth with MPCP DEREG.
The same EPON0/3 port has seven surviving ONUs online with RX values from -21.89 to -18.21 dBm and TX values around +2.35 to +2.51 dBm, so the port and shared splitter are functioning.
The OLT population shows 185 online and only 7 offline out of 192, which is not consistent with all PONs failing.

The subscriber's historical RX, TX, bias current, distance, supply voltage, and temperature were stable and healthy before telemetry collection stopped; there is no evidence of fibre degradation, laser degradation, or distance change.
The session count is only 1 in 24 hours and the average duration is about 699 minutes, so there is no session flapping or authentication-driven fault.
The customer VLAN is correctly provisioned as VLAN 1113, and the RADIUS record matches CRM, so this is not a missing-entry, suspended-service, line-ID conflict, or VLAN 46 fault.
The health-check result claiming all 7 PONs failed is contradicted by the direct ONU and OLT probes and should be corrected as a monitoring defect.

remediation.action: Treat customer 29732 as offline and dispatch ONU/CPE and access-fibre troubleshooting: verify power, cabling, LOS indicators, and optical levels at the premises, then re-register or replace the ONU if required. Separately investigate and correct the health-check aggregation that reported all 7 PONs failed despite 185 of 192 ONUs being online and the OLT responding normally.

ground_truth.root_cause: The health check samples one ONU per PON port, preferring ONU id 1. On several ports the id 1 ONU happens to be offline for individual reasons, so each port is marked failed and the OLT is reported critical. The ports and the OLT are serving normally; one customer is genuinely offline.
expected_reasoning: The alarm claims all seven PONs failed on this OLT
The failed_pons_list names ONU index 1 on every port, which is the check's preferred sample
Probing the rest of EPON0/3 shows 27 of 28 ONUs online with normal RX and TX
So the port is serving and only the sampled ONU is down
oid_subtree_responds is true and the probe returns definite answers, ruling out the firmware mechanism
OLT ping, SNMP, CPU, memory, temperature and 33 days of uptime are all normal
CRM offline count across the OLT is consistent with the 4.85% background rate
The subject ONU last held a session three days ago and its traffic has been zero since
The alarm is a sampling artifact; the only real fault is one customer offline for three days

expected_escalation.review_reason: The health check's one-ONU-per-port sampling produced a false OLT-wide critical; monitoring should be raised separately

distractors: An OLT-wide critical invites a Disaster conclusion
Every port genuinely reports a failed sample, so the alarm looks internally consistent
There is a real fault here, so dismissing the alarm entirely would also miss it
